title: Formalize the async consolidation worker + EVERY_N cadence throttling
summary: Replace the metadata-flag polling hack with a real consolidated_at column + claim-based locking; throttle inline consolidation to every Nth write.
description:
Two related changes to the existing consolidation pipeline. (1) `scripts/consolidate_pending.py` currently finds pending rows via a `metadata.consolidated: false` JSON flag — its own docstring already flags this as a stand-in, not a production implementation. Add a `consolidated_at TIMESTAMP` (nullable) column to `working_memory`/`episodic_memory` via a new migration, switch the eligibility filter to `WHERE consolidated_at IS NULL`, and add a claim-based update (`UPDATE ... SET consolidated_at = ? WHERE id = ? AND consolidated_at IS NULL`, checking rowcount) so two concurrent worker instances can't double-process the same row — the basic idempotency/locking the script's own docstring says a real implementation needs. (2) Add an optional `consolidate_every_n: int = 1` setting on `MemoryStore` (default 1 = today's behavior — consolidate on every write) so the *inline* synchronous consolidator only fires every Nth `remember()` call per scope, reducing LLM-call cost on the hot write path. Also have the worker script optionally invoke the new Reconciler (ENH-3) every `--dedup-every-n` batches.

Inspired by: the Agent Memory Toolkit's `FACT_EXTRACTION_EVERY_N`/`THREAD_SUMMARY_EVERY_N`/`DEDUP_EVERY_N` env-var-driven cadence, and its change-feed-triggered Durable Functions tier for offloading processing off the write path.

Db2 feasibility — this is the "adapt, don't skip" item: Db2 LUW has no native change-feed mechanism equivalent to Cosmos DB's, so the Durable Functions tier can't be ported directly. This worker (polling + a claim column) is the Db2-appropriate substitute — same underlying goal (async, off-the-hot-path processing), different mechanism. Builds entirely on the existing script and existing MemoryStore/Consolidator machinery — no new infrastructure, no new external service dependency, keeping the Step 0 "zero mandatory external services" principle intact. Depends on ENH-3 for the Reconciler-integration half; the consolidated_at/locking half can ship independently.

comments.text: Done. (1) Migration 0005: consolidated_at TIMESTAMP (nullable, indexed on agent_id) added to working_memory and episodic_memory only — these are the consolidation inputs; the other three tables are outputs. (2) _HAS_CONSOLIDATED_AT class-attribute gate on BaseRepository (mirrors _HAS_SUPERSESSION pattern) ensures SQL never references the column on tables that lack it (Db2 SQLCODE -206 guard). (3) BaseRepository._claim_consolidated(): issues UPDATE ... SET consolidated_at = ? WHERE id = ? AND consolidated_at IS NULL and checks rowcount — rowcount 0 means another worker already claimed the row, skip; rowcount 1 means this worker owns it. Db2 row-level locking serializes competing UPDATEs at the engine level. (4) MemoryStore.consolidate_every_n=N: in-memory per-scope counter (keyed by agent_id/user_id/thread_id) fires the inline consolidator every Nth remember() call. Default 1 = existing behaviour. Limitation documented: counter resets on process restart, not shared across multiple app instances. (5) scripts/consolidate_pending.py rewritten: eligibility filter is now consolidated_at IS NULL (drops the JSON_VALUE flag hack); uses _claim_consolidated() for locking; adds --reconciler-module/class/--dedup-every-n to invoke the ENH-3 Reconciler every N batches. Worker is documented as the Db2-appropriate substitute for Cosmos change-feed/Durable Functions — no new external service dependency. (6) 35 new unit tests in tests/test_enh4.py; 395 total pass. ruff clean. DECISIONS.md entry appended.
